summary: The #retravel extended-command row reaches C cmd.c:doextcmd(), which calls its selected function pointer and returns that function's ECMD result. The row at cmd.c:1832 points to dotravel_target(); with travelcc unset, that helper prints 'No travel destination set.' and returns ECMD_OK. JavaScript already ports that helper and the row, but doextcmd()'s dispatch switch omits dotravel_target, so its default resets command variables and throws before the C guard runs.

source.branch: When doextcmd() selects the retravel row (cmd.c:1832) while travelcc is unset, C invokes dotravel_target(), which prints the no-destination message and returns ECMD_OK.
callers: rhack() dispatches the '#' row to doextcmd() (cmd.c:3732-3751)
extcmdlist[] registers retravel with dotravel_target as ef_funct (cmd.c:1832); doextcmd() calls the selected function pointer and returns its ECMD result (cmd.c:493-519)

evidence: C source: nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:493-519 assigns extcmdlist[idx].ef_funct, sets ge.ext_tlist, invokes (*func)(), and returns its result; cmd.c:1832 maps the retravel row to dotravel_target().
C source: nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:5348-5355 checks travelcc with isok(); an unset destination prints 'No travel destination set.' and returns ECMD_OK without entering movement or consuming RNG.

JavaScript source: js/cmd.js:2739-2745 already implements the unset-destination guard and message. js/cmd.js:5004-5422 dispatches selected extended-command functions, but has no dotravel_target case; the default at 5419-5422 resets command variables and raises UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError.

Recorded evidence: immutable Prep50 delivery 6289b66eab4b8f23dfd1d8a0ed751bbc02997d5ffe16be9108e72846f27add37 reports an independent byte-identical patched-C replay and accepted-source comparison. The delegated prefix matches 11 screens/cursors and all 2819 RNG calls; the error occurs when step 11 dispatches retravel.

Implementation scope is the missing dotravel_target branch in the existing cmd.c:doextcmd() port plus focused command-dispatch coverage. The helper itself is already implemented; no C callee or shared state contract needs a new port.
